description: Recent EXECUTED trades (the fills tape) for a Polymarket market — actual money that changed hands, newest first. Each trade: side (BUY/SELL), outcome (Yes/No or the option name), outcome_index, size (shares), price (that fill's OWN outcome's price), unix, timestamp, and the trader's wallet/pseudonym. Use for "what's the recent order flow", "is smart money buying Yes", "how much just traded and at what price". DISTINCT from polymarket_orderbook (resting/unfilled orders — intent) and polymarket_price_history (the CP time-series). Pass a market slug or numeric id (same input as polymarket_market). PAGING: `limit` goes to 1000; follow `next_cursor` to walk further back. To measure a whole time window rather than the tail (e.g. what takers actually paid across one 15-minute crypto window) pass `window_start` (+ `window_end`): the tool walks the tape back to the window start itself and returns `coverage` saying whether the walk reached it or ran out of page budget, plus a size-weighted `per_minute` fill-price summary on the first outcome's side.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's `next_cursor` — continues the newest-first tape further back. Omit for the newest page. Ignored in window mode.

limit.description: Trades per page / trades returned, 1-1000 (default 20; in window mode default 100).

max_pages.description: Window mode only: page budget, 1-20 (default 8, 1000 fills each). If the walk hits it before reaching window_start, coverage.complete is false.

slug_or_id.description: Market slug (e.g. "will-trump-win-2024") or numeric id — same input as polymarket_market.

window_end.description: ISO datetime or epoch seconds, exclusive (default: now). Only used with window_start.

window_start.description: ISO datetime or epoch seconds. Switches to window mode: walks the whole tape back to this instant. Inclusive.
